name: Romanian

ancestors.notes: Balkan Romance Vulgar Latin: Eastern Romance branch with no lenition, central vowels, postposed article.

Slavic superstrate (7th c. onwards): massive lexical influence (~40% of vocabulary), some phonological impact (palatalisation patterns, possible influence on central vowels). Old Church Slavonic was the literary/liturgical language until 16th–17th c.
Dacian/Thracian substrate: ~100+ words shared with Albanian of unknown origin (copil, moș, viezure). Possible influence on central vowels /ə, ɨ/ and postposed article.
Greek adstrate: Byzantine influence, shared Balkan sprachbund features.
Turkish adstrate (14th–19th c.): lexical borrowings from Ottoman period.
Hungarian adstrate: centuries of contact in Transylvania. Lexical exchange.

notes: Standard Romanian. Eastern Romance, the ONLY Romance language east of the Adriatic. Key features: (1) Central vowels /ə/ (⟨ă⟩) and /ɨ/ (⟨â/î⟩) — unique in Romance. (2) NO intervocalic lenition (lup, foc — not *lub, *fogo). (3) Postposed definite article (lupul 'the wolf'). (4) Rich diphthong/triphthong system. (5) Rhotacism: intervocalic /l/ → /r/ in some words (soare < SOLEM). (6) Massive Slavic vocabulary layer (~40%). (7) Balkan sprachbund member (Chițoran 2001, Sala 2005). (8) Word-initial ⟨e⟩ is [je] in a closed, cited set: the personal pronouns ⟨eu el ea ei ele⟩ and the present/imperfect forms of ⟨a fi⟩ (⟨e este ești era erai eram erați erau⟩) — everywhere else word-initial ⟨e⟩ is [e] (⟨elev⟩, ⟨examen⟩); this is lexical, so it lives in word_exceptions (DOOM3; Chitoran 2002 ch. 2). (9) ⟨ă⟩ is declared in vowel_graphemes because the engine's closed Latin letter inventory does not carry it; without that declaration every vowel-conditioned rule fails next to it (⟨băieți⟩, ⟨păi⟩). STRESS EXEMPTION (research/production tier rule): Romanian lexical stress is phonemic but NOT predictable from standard orthography (cópii 'copies' vs copíi 'children' are spelled identically); the standard norm writes no stress marks, so the spec carries no stress block per docs/quality_tiers.md. CEILING: after ⟨c g⟩ a following ⟨i⟩ before a vowel is silent in inherited vocabulary (⟨cioban⟩ [tʃoˈban]) but syllabic in the neologistic layer (⟨Dacia⟩ [ˈdatʃi.a], ⟨sociologie⟩); the split is lexical, not orthographic, so the spec emits the majority syllabic reading and leaves the rest to a caller-supplied lexicon.

allophone_rules.notes: ⟨c⟩ is /tʃ/ before ⟨e i⟩; ⟨ch⟩ keeps /k/ (its own grapheme). Chitoran 2002 ch. 2; DOOM3.
⟨g⟩ is /dʒ/ before ⟨e i⟩; ⟨gh⟩ keeps /ɡ/ (its own grapheme). Chitoran 2002 ch. 2; DOOM3.

Word-initial prevocalic /i/ has no onset available and surfaces as the glide [j] — ⟨iarnă⟩ [ˈjarnə], ⟨ied⟩ [jed], ⟨iute⟩ [ˈjute] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 3, glide formation; Vasiliu 1965). A glide needs a nucleus after it and the word needs one at all, so the rule is blocked before another ⟨i⟩ and on a word with no other nucleus: ⟨ii⟩ is [ij], never [jj] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 3; Hayes 2009 ch. 13).

Post-vocalic ⟨i⟩ is the glide [j], falling in a diphthong (⟨mai⟩ [maj], ⟨doi⟩ [doj], ⟨căi⟩ [kəj]) or in the onset of the next syllable (⟨baie⟩ [ˈbaje], ⟨ploaie⟩ [ˈplo̯aje]); the plural+article ⟨-ii⟩ is [ij] (⟨copii⟩ [koˈpij]). Post-consonantal ⟨i⟩ is NOT covered: there it is syllabic and stands in hiatus (⟨Românie⟩ [romɨˈni.e], ⟨abația⟩ [abaˈtsi.a]) — Chitoran 2002 ch. 3. A glide needs a nucleus after it and the word needs one at all, so the rule is blocked before another ⟨i⟩ and on a word with no other nucleus: ⟨ii⟩ is [ij], never [jj] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 3; Hayes 2009 ch. 13).

The word-final desinential ⟨i⟩ (plural, 2sg) is asyllabic: it deletes and palatalizes the preceding consonant — ⟨lupi⟩ [lupʲ], ⟨pomi⟩ [pomʲ], ⟨ochi⟩ [okʲ], ⟨vezi⟩ [vezʲ] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 5, 'final devoiced i'; Renwick 2014; DOOM3). `requires_other_nucleus` keeps the monosyllables that have no other vowel intact — ⟨și⟩ [ʃi], ⟨fi⟩ [fi], ⟨zi⟩ [zi]. Liquids are excluded here and handled by RO_FINAL_I_ASYLLABIC_LIQUID so that the muta cum liquida cluster keeps a syllabic [i].

The same desinence after a liquid, but ONLY where the liquid is not the second member of a muta cum liquida onset: ⟨adevăruri⟩ [adeˈvərurʲ], ⟨fii⟩-type aside. After obstruent+liquid the /i/ must be syllabic because the glide cannot join a complex onset — ⟨noștri⟩ [ˈnoʃtri], ⟨codri⟩ [ˈkodri], ⟨acri⟩ [ˈakri] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 3 and ch. 5, on muta cum liquida; DOOM3).
